axis: dull local soreness → extreme, torture-grade pain

members.tone: The plain term of the family - it reports that something hurts, in the body or in the mind, without saying how sharply or how much.
Low and unbroken - a pain with no edge on it, the opposite of the sting in *biting*.
Informal where *aching* is plain, and the shortened shape keeps the same dull, steady pain small.
Turned outward - it describes the look or the cry that shows pain, agony included, not the thing doing the hurting.
The British spelling of *agonized* and identical in force - distress made visible rather than inflicted.
Far past *aching* - the pain is extreme, and the word lends it agony's whole weight.
The British spelling of *agonizing*, with the same extremity and no softening.
The absolute of the set - it admits no degree above itself, so anything short of unbearable is overstated by it.
Extremity felt as an ordeal - where *excruciating* measures the pain, this measures what it costs whoever goes through it.
Extremity cast as an act - the pain is not merely present but done to someone, which *excruciating* never says.
The quality without the agent - pain of the order torture produces, said of the experience rather than of anyone inflicting it.
The heavier build beside *torturous* - identical extremity, carried in a more laboured word.
Sharp and stinging where *aching* is dull, and cold above all is what it is said of.
The same sharp sting held as a condition rather than an act - a bitter cold surrounds you where a biting one goes at you.
Small and local - the soreness of skin rubbed raw, at the shallow end of everything else here.
Blunter than *chafed* for the same abraded skin, with the sore itself in view rather than the rubbing that made it.
